req.title: Reject wrong method on /put
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PUT on /put.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /put must return HTTP 405 for any method other than PUT. We need: (1) a positive test confirming PUT returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming GET/POST/DELETE/PATCH return 405, and (3) boundary tests at the method-selection boundary. Mutation resilience requires exact status code assertions (405 not >=400), testing both sides of the allowed-method check, and verifying the Allow header contains PUT. We cover EP (PUT vs non-PUT partition), NEG (wrong methods), BVA (adjacent methods like PATCH which has its own route), and DT (decision table of method -> status code).

tests.name: test_put_method_returns_200_on_put_endpoint
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: Response body is JSON containing url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json keys
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: PUT on /put must succeed with 2xx
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_put_method_returns_200_on_put_endpoint():
    r = client.put('/put')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data

test_put_method_returns_200_on_put_endpoint()

tests.name: test_put_with_json_body_returns_200_and_correct_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send HTTP PUT request to /put with JSON body {"key": "value"}
expected: Response JSON contains 'json' key with value {"key": "value"}
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: PUT on /put with body returns 200 and echoes JSON payload
tests.executable:
import json
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_put_with_json_body_returns_200_and_correct_payload():
    payload = {"key": "value"}
    r = client.put(
        '/put',
        data=json.dumps(payload),
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert data['json'] == {"key": "value"}
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'args' in data
    assert 'headers' in data

test_put_with_json_body_returns_200_and_correct_payload()

tests.name: test_multiple_wrong_methods_all_return_405_on_put_endpoint
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET, POST, DELETE, PATCH requests to /put in sequence
expected: All non-PUT methods return exactly HTTP 405
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: Decision table — every non-PUT method maps to 405
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_multiple_wrong_methods_all_return_405_on_put_endpoint():
    wrong_methods = [
        client.get,
        client.post,
        client.delete,
        client.patch,
    ]
    for method_fn in wrong_methods:
        r = method_fn('/put')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"Expected 405 but got {r.status_code} for {method_fn}"
        assert r.status_code != 200
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 500

test_multiple_wrong_methods_all_return_405_on_put_endpoint()

tests.name: test_put_returns_200_not_405_confirming_method_boundary
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
PUT is the only allowed method — boundary between allowed and disallowed
actions: Send PUT to /put and assert exactly 200
Send GET to /put and assert exactly 405 to confirm the boundary
trace: R-HTTPBIN-007: BVA boundary — PUT=200, GET=405 confirms exact method boundary
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_put_returns_200_not_405_confirming_method_boundary():
    r_put = client.put('/put')
    assert r_put.status_code == 200
    assert r_put.status_code != 405

    r_get = client.get('/put')
    assert r_get.status_code == 405
    assert r_get.status_code != 200

    assert r_put.status_code != r_get.status_code

test_put_returns_200_not_405_confirming_method_boundary()
